structure: Each person's two-dimensional measurement at visit t is mean + stable component + visit deviation. Independent Gaussian draws implement this additive model. The records identify total same-visit covariance but not its allocation between stable and visit-specific components; this generator chooses one feasible allocation.

parameter_provenance.basis: Reported population means; deviations have zero mean.
Diagonal entries of the stable-component covariance matrix.
Diagonal entries of each visit-deviation covariance matrix.

parameter_provenance.value: Stable components independent of deviations; deviations independent across visits; persons independent.
parameter_provenance.basis: Stipulated measurement-model independence, allowing X-Y dependence within each component vector.

parameter_provenance.parameter: within-person X-Y covariance at each visit
parameter_provenance.basis: Chosen feasible scenario; not determined by the records.
Conditional on the chosen within covariance: 2.6 - 0.6 = 2.0.
Convenient sampling distributions; no Gaussian shape is supplied by the records.

requested_estimands.name: change_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: Stable components cancel in changes. Independent visits give change variances 2 and change covariance 2 * 0.6 = 1.2, hence correlation 0.6. The within-person covariance is not identified.

requested_estimands.name: same_visit_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: Directly reported by B. The model reproduces it at both visits: (2.0 + 0.6) / 5 = 0.52. This identification does not require Gaussian distributions.

requested_estimands.name: cross_visit_correlation
requested_estimands.basis: Independent visit deviations leave only stable-component cross-covariance: Corr(X_visit1,Y_visit2) = 2.0 / 5 = 0.4. Its value depends on the unidentified covariance allocation.

limitations: These are artificial population constraints, not clinical evidence or biomedical validation.

Writing w for within-person X-Y covariance, the records imply between-person covariance 2.6 - w. Every w in [-1,1] is feasible. Thus change correlation can range from -1 to 1, while cross-visit correlation ranges from 0.32 to 0.72.
The two unidentified functionals are linked: change_correlation + 5 * cross_visit_correlation = 2.6.
Despite the standardized-unit description, the stipulated measurement variance is 5, not 1; the generator preserves the supplied component variances.
Finite random samples will not exactly match population moments. No sample adjustment, selection, or favorable-seed search is used.
The generator has not been executed or empirically validated here.
